Decision for the owner: normalize generation naming on GD and GE across body kits and hoods, which today say MC, 2007, GD, GE and GK interchangeably.
Honda S2000111001000000000One sheet kit, one true kit, one product, and it is the strongest listing in the whole group: 9 of 11 molds live across 44 variants. Missing are the front bumper insert 1538 and one of the two front fenders, since the sheet carries both an OEM-width and a widebody fender but the product offers a single 'Front Fender'. No duplicates, fragments or orphans. Decision for the owner: split the front fender into OEM and widebody options so buyers cannot order the wrong arch.
Hyundai Tucson1100000010000001 sheet kit (one grille mold), zero store products. Old code block and a chassis that does not fit the JDM/Euro catalog. Owner decision: leave unlisted.
Lamborghini Aventador4400000040000004 sheet kits, zero store products: the entire Aventador range is unlisted. Best candidates to publish are the Novitec GT-wing set (4 numbered molds) and the DMC carbon set. Two flags: the 750.0 label is a stray price that reads as the LP750/SV look, and code 2358 is double-booked with the Ferrari 599. Owner decision: whether exotics get a catalog presence at all.
Lamborghini Gallardo3300000021000003 sheet kits, zero store products. Only K375 (Super Trofeo style) reads as a genuine catalog kit; the other two are tagged to specific customer cars (the green car, Vattana's race car). Owner decision: publish the Super Trofeo set and leave the two one-offs off the catalog.
Lamborghini Huracan2200000020000002 sheet kits, zero store products, both fully missing from the catalog. All 7 molds are numbered so both are ready to list. Owner decision: whether the Euro label is a brand that can be named publicly.
Lexus GS300111010000000000One sheet row, one live product, complete. Nothing missing or duplicated. The listing is a single diffuser sold as a Body Kit at $895-$1030, which is the only thing worth fixing. Owner decision: retitle to Front Diffuser, and decide whether a GS300 chassis with four live carbon hood and roof listings deserves a real kit.
Lexus IS250222011000000000Two sheet kits, both live, but the Blitz product is short one piece: the carbon front-lip cover 001441/1 is molded and not sold. The two kits together make a full car (Blitz front, TOM'S rear and sides) which is worth saying on both PDPs. Both titles carry a Toyota prefix on a Lexus. Owner decision: add the carbon lip cover as a component or confirm it is a shop-only part.
Lexus LS430233020000100000K329 is three kits in one auto-group and splits cleanly at the code jumps: the Vertex 5-piece kit (947-951), the Vertex face-off front end (1361-1363), and the ETi face-off front end (1469-1470, which absorbs K330). All three are live and all sheet pieces are present. The live problem is naming: two products are called Face Off VERTEX Style Body Kit with only ETi separating them, and one ships without a bumper. Owner decision: rename the ETi face-off (fender plus hood, bumper reused) so a customer cannot buy the wrong front end.
Lexus RX111000000100000One sheet kit, one live product, all recorded pieces present. The open issue is a piece-count mismatch: the sheet calls it an 8-piece Branew skirt kit and the storefront repeats that in tags, but only three part rows (front lip, rear lip, side skirt) exist. On a $3,220 top variant that is a real shortage risk. Owner decision: confirm the true Branew piece count with the factory, then either add the missing rows or drop 8pcs from the tag.
Lotus Exige/Elise1100000010000001 sheet kit, zero store products. An in-house ETi widebody with four numbered molds is unlisted, and it carries no third-party brand exposure. Owner decision: this is a low-risk own-design listing, publish or park it.
Maserati1100000001000001 sheet kit, zero store products, and the sheet rows are barely usable: no Maserati model, no part category, plus two rows of unrelated debris. Owner decision: have the shop identify what molds 3524-3526 actually are before anything else.
Mazda 2001000000000010No Mazda 2 kits in the sheet and one store product, an ETi carbon spoiler with no sheet source. Nothing missing, nothing duplicated. Only action is a title cleanup on the spoiler ('MAZDA2 2 ETi' reads as a generation error).
Mazda 35560400010202005 sheet kits, 4 of them live and 1 missing (K127, the second Mazdaspeed grille+spoiler pair, probably the 4-door set). The real problem is duplication and pricing: both the Mazdaspeed and the AutoExe kits are listed twice, once as proper component products and once as opaque '5 DOOR' bundles priced roughly 4x higher. Two more products are single pieces titled 'Body Kit' (Varis spoiler, RE-Amemiya gap spoiler). Owner decision: which of each duplicate pair survives, and whether the 5-door bundle prices or the component prices are correct.
Mazda MX-5111000001000100One sheet kit (K110, front bumper + rear bumper + side skirt, codes 384-386) and one store product, and they do not match. The live 'Standard Style Body Kit' sells a taillight and a duckbill with no sheet source, so the actual MX-5 kit is effectively missing while a mislabelled product occupies its name. Owner decision: build out K110's three pieces under this product or rename it and stop calling it a body kit.
McLaren 720S3300000030000003 sheet kits, zero store products. A full RYFT front-end set (7 pieces) plus two competing GT spoilers (RYFT and Novitec) are all unlisted. One code error to fix (354 vs 3546). Owner decision: whether McLaren is a market ETi wants, and if so sell the RYFT spoiler and front set as one product.
Mercedes C-Class W205110000001000000Zero store products against a complete 6-mold W205 kit. Two ETi W205 hoods are already live, so the chassis exists in the catalog and the kit would have somewhere to sit. Owner decision: confirm the kit is the SR66 Design style before naming it that publicly, or list it as an ETi design.
Mercedes CLK W209110000001000000Zero store products against a complete 9-mold Prior Design widebody for the CLK W209. Nothing to reconcile - this is a straight build-it decision. Codes 3081-3089 sit immediately before the W205 block (3127-3132), so both Mercedes gaps came from the same unbuilt stretch of the sheet.
Mercedes CLS C257111001000000000One kit, live, 4 of 5 molds built out. Add the ETi rear diffuser (3264) as a second Rear Diffuser option. The sheet block has no brand label at all, so the CLS53 AMG naming came from the store side and looks right.
Mercedes S-Class W140777061000000000Seven sheet kits, seven products, six clean one-to-one maps - the tidiest block in the group. The only real issue is the two ETi Skirt products: the sheet gives Skirt 1 a front skirt (597) and Skirt 2 a front + rear pair (199/200), but the store sells one front and one rear, so front skirt 199 is unaccounted for. Owner decision: are 597 and 199 the same mold - if yes, merge into one W140 ETi Skirt Kit.
Mercedes S-Class W220111110000010000One kit, complete and live. A duplicate draft of the same Wald kit sits alongside it, tagged BMW with a bmw- handle. Archive the draft, no other action.
Mercedes SL R129111010000000000One kit, complete and live. Only cleanup is the Front Fender component name, which is really a front flare trim (1428). Handle says W129 where the chassis is R129.
Mercedes SLR111010000000000One kit, complete and live, nothing missing. Only the title overstates the contents: two front pieces sold as a Body Kit.
Mini F55/F563300000030000003 sheet kits, zero store products. The Duell AG rear-end kit (7 molds) is a complete sellable product with nothing live. The whole Mini range across F5x/R56/R53 is absent from the store. Owner decision: Mini is a real Thai/EU market, decide whether to open the range with the Duell AG kit.
Mini R531100000010000001 sheet kit, zero store products. Five molds exist but three have blank descriptions, so the kit contents are unknown. Owner decision: have the shop name molds 2431/2432/2434 before anything is listed.
Mini R563300000030000003 sheet kits, zero store products. The ETi W-1 6-piece carbon set is complete on paper and unlisted. Nothing to deduplicate. Owner decision: whether ETi's own Mini designs are worth publishing given they carry the ETi name rather than a licensed brand.
Mitsubishi Evo 6001000000000010No Evo 6 kits in the sheet and only one store product, an OEM carbon spoiler with no sheet source. Two standalone Evo 6 door products also exist outside the kit list. Nothing to reconcile; the chassis is aero-thin in the catalogue and would need a separate source list if Nate wants to build it out.
Mitsubishi FTO222020000000000Two sheet kits, two store products, exact one-to-one mapping with no duplicates, fragments or gaps. Neither is a full body kit: Bozz Speed supplies the front bumper and spoiler, Kaze supplies the side skirt and rear bumper. Cross-sell them as a pair and fix both titles, which currently promise a complete kit. No hoods, trunks or doors exist for FTO in the store at all.
Mitsubishi GTO / 3000GT666031100102000Six sheet kits, six store products, no drafts and no duplicates - the cleanest chassis in the group. Two real gaps: the ETi Widebody GT (K158) is live with only 7 of its 13 pieces, and the C-West block (K155) is split over two products with the front fender 1365 missing entirely. The 91-93 / 94-97 / 99 generation split comes from store titles, not the sheet, and the ETi rear skirt 570 sits on the 91-93 product while its mold code belongs to the 99 block. Owner decision: complete the Widebody GT piece list, and confirm which generation rear skirt 570 actually fits.
Mitsubishi Lancer EX320000002000000Three sheet kits, zero store products - the only chassis in the group with no listings at all. All three are Evo X face-conversion parts for the Lancer EX: two front bumper molds (1133 and 1235) that the Evo X Step 1 and Step 2 kits are actually built on, plus a Varis side skirt. The conversion is a real sellable product and is currently invisible to Lancer EX owners, who cannot find it under an Evo X title. Owner decision: create a Lancer EX conversion product, and resolve the 1235 code collision between the K142 bumper and the K146 side skirt first.
Mitsubishi Space Wagon113010000010000One sheet kit, fully live with all eight pieces in a single product - structurally the healthiest listing in the group. The only question is the two standalone spoilers: one duplicates the kit component, the other is a V2 with no sheet row and identical pricing. Owner decision: confirm whether the V2 spoiler is a real second mold or a stale copy.
Mitsubishi Triton121011000000000The only sheet kit here, K128, is an auto-grouping error: it welds the Lancer EX to Evo X conversion V2 (codes 1190-1191) onto the Triton 2022 kit (codes 3441-3443) across a 2,250-code jump. Split into two true kits, both live - the Triton half as P10727221395737 and the conversion half as P10626079621401 in the Evo X packet. The Triton product collapses the sheet's two door sets into one generic 'Door' component. No duplicates or unsourced products on this chassis.
NON-AERO (excluded)0050000000000505 products swept into the aero packets by product type, none of them body kit items and none with a sheet source. Two (hatch upgrade, shipping protection) are deliberate add-on SKUs and should stay. The other three (2JZ swap kit, seat belt, carbon seats) are real products in the wrong catalog bucket. Owner decision: none needed beyond retyping so future audits stop flagging them.
Nissan 300ZX Z323330300000001003 sheet kits, 3 store products, all live and correctly mapped, no missing molds and no duplicates. The God Father widebody carries all 9 molds and the sheet's 13 pcs label is just the paired-side count. Only cleanup is naming: the Trust product holds one front bumper but is titled Body Kit, and the God Father kit uses component names (Fender, Cover, Lighting) a customer cannot decode. Nothing here needs an owner decision beyond approving the renames.
Nissan Cefiro A312220110000000002 sheet kits, both live, no duplicates and no unsourced products. The 5-piece ETi kit is complete; the ETi widebody product carries only 3 of its 7 pieces, missing rear door fender 975, front bumper 1066, rear bumper 1067 and side skirt 1068. No R32 face-off kit exists on either the sheet side or the store side for this chassis, so there is nothing to reconcile there and nothing should be invented. Owner decision: add the 4 missing widebody pieces or confirm the A31 widebody is deliberately sold as a fender-only conversion.
Nissan Juke44111211000430204 sheet kits, all 4 represented on the site, but only Ken Style and Nismo Design are clean. The ETi kit K164 is fragmented across 4 products and its eyebrow trims 3206/3207 sit inside a product wrongly named ETi Nismo Style Standard; the Impul spoiler and the Nismo spoiler are each listed twice (kit product plus standalone carbon spoiler). Two fender products have no sheet source: the OEM one is a normal carbon panel, the Nismo Style Design one is likely the ETi fender 1764 relabeled. Owner decision: fold K164's five pieces into one ETi Juke kit and rule once on whether spoilers and fenders stay as a-la-carte singles alongside the kits.
Nissan Navara1120100000000101 sheet kit, a single ETi front bumper 2315, live and correct. No duplicates, no fragments, no missing pieces; the only other product is an OEM-shape carbon fender with no source in this bodykit sheet, which is normal for panel products. Owner decision: rename the single-bumper listing from Body Kit to Front Bumper so the catalog stops promising a kit that does not exist.
Nissan Skyline (other)001000000000010No sheet kits exist for this bucket, so there is nothing to reconcile. The single store product is a BMW E46 Hamann GTR kit and the reference list adds a Honda Civic EK GTR hood, both matched on the string GTR rather than on chassis. Action is on the matcher, not the catalog: exclude GTR as a chassis token for Skyline and re-bucket both products to their real chassis.
Porsche 7182230101000010002 sheet kits, both live, none missing. The GT3 conversion is fragmented: its rear bumper is a separate product called Factory. Same shared canard piece (2297/2) is unlisted here as it is on 997 and 981. Owner decision: merge the Factory rear bumper into the GT3 Conversion product.
Porsche 9815690411000220005 auto-kits settle into 6 true kits after splitting K356 into the early 3-piece Boxster GT4 set and the later 8-piece GT4 conversion. All 6 are live in some form, none MISSING, but the GT4 conversion is cut across two products with inverted names and the 718 conversion is listed twice (Corsa vs Face Off) at two prices. Owner decision: merge the GT4/Factory pair into one product and kill one of the two 718 conversion listings.
Porsche 986/987546220200030000Sheet holds 5 auto-kits that settle into 4 true kits (918 Spyder + Rapica merge into the one Replica kit). All 4 are live, but the GT1/GT3 RS widebody and the Techart widebody are each listed 3-4 times under different names and at wildly different prices ($12500 vs $26995-$29900). The only properly itemized products are drafts. Owner decision: which name and which price is the real one for the GT1 widebody and for the Techart widebody, then publish the itemized drafts over the sold-as-kit actives.
Porsche 9912220110000000002 sheet kits, 2 true kits, both live and correctly named, the cleanest chassis in this group. Only gap is the Techart front diffuser centre plate (3074/2). Nothing missing, no duplicates, no drafts.
Porsche 996111000000100000Single 996 sheet row (a wing side blade) against a single live product priced like a complete wing. No duplicates, nothing missing. Owner decision: confirm whether the 996 GT3 RS product ships a full wing assembly or just the side blades, and reprice or rename accordingly.
Porsche 9973340101001020003 sheet kits, 3 true kits, all live. The GT3 conversion is fragmented across a bumper-only product and a chassis-less Euro Hour Conversion product that actually holds its lip and canards. Prior Design is fine on the active side but has three duplicate Porsche 2009 drafts sitting in the unclassified pile. Owner decision: whether the shared GT3 conversion lip + canards (2296/2297) are one universal add-on product or duplicated per chassis (997/981/718).
Porsche Cayenne2230200000000002 sheet kits, both live, nothing missing. Third active product (Gravis) is an ETi house name with no sheet source and most likely the Lumma widebody under a rebrand. Both real kits sell as single SKUs with zero piece breakdown, so no Cayenne trim can be bought a la carte. Owner decision: is Gravis the Lumma kit or a separate design.
Porsche Panamera1110001000010001 sheet kit, live but only 20 percent of it: four of the five pieces are stranded in a draft filed under Taycan. No duplicates, nothing genuinely missing from the mold list. Owner decision: approve the merge and publish the full 5-piece Panamera set.
Porsche Taycan111110000000100Only 1 real Taycan sheet kit (the ZYRT lip) and it is live. The second Taycan product is a draft holding four Panamera diffusers under the wrong chassis. Owner decision: confirm the 3290-3293 diffusers are Panamera, then merge that draft into the Panamera listing.
Subaru Legacy110000001000000A single ETi rear lip mold (704) and no store product: the Legacy is missing entirely. It sits between the GC8 rows in the sheet, which suggests a BE/BH-era car, but the generation is not recorded. Owner decision: confirm the fitment year with the factory before spending a listing on a one-piece Legacy item, it is the lowest-value gap in this group.
Tesla002100000000030No Tesla kits in the sheet; the 3 store products are from the separate dry-carbon line. Two are live, one (eyelid canards) is a stranded draft with no Tesla tags. Owner decision: publish or archive the canard draft so the Model 3 range is consistent.
Toyota Alphard 30444040000000000Cleanest chassis in the group: 4 sheet kits, 4 live products, one to one, no merges, splits, duplicates or missing pieces. The whole finding here is brand spelling, and it is customer-facing on premium-van money (top variant $3,475): Silk Blade should be Silk Blaze and Kulk Racing should be Kuhl Racing. Owner decision: approve the two brand renames, or confirm the misspellings are deliberate to keep distance from the Japanese brands.
Toyota Altezza / Lexus IS300222020000000000Two sheet kits, two live products, both complete against the sheet. Nothing missing, duplicated or fragmented. The only risk is expectation: both listings are called Body Kit while one is a single lip and the other is a lip plus skirts, with no rear pieces anywhere in the sheet for this chassis. Owner decision: retitle to Front Lip / Front Lip and Side Skirt Kit, or commission the missing C-West rear.
Toyota Camry460700141002010Four auto-kits resolve into 6 true kits after two splits (K300 hides a standalone factory spoiler, K302 hides a second widened bumper pair). Not one Camry product is live: all 7 are drafts, so commercially this chassis does not exist today. One kit is fragmented (VIP1 split across the VIP1 and Full Bumper listings) and one is fully missing (widened OEM bumpers 1251-1252). Owner decision: publish or kill the Camry line as a block, and if publishing, merge VIP1 first and retitle the two single-piece listings so they do not read as kits.
Toyota Fortuner113010000000020One sheet kit, one live product, complete. The two OEM carbon fender listings have no bodykit-sheet source (they come off the carbon parts list) and look like the same part sold twice under Fortuner-only and Revo / Fortuner fitment. Owner decision: confirm whether the Revo and Fortuner front fenders share a mold and collapse to a single listing if so.
Toyota Harrier111010000000100One sheet kit, one live product, all three pieces present, so nothing is missing. The product is mislabelled: it sells as Standard when the sheet rows are Ken Style, and that mismatch is why neither side produced a candidate match automatically. Owner decision: approve the rename to Ken Style and fix the Front Diffuse component typo.
Toyota Hilux Vigo111010000000000One sheet kit, one live product, complete. No missing pieces, duplicates or fragments. The only defect is taxonomy: the product is typed Side Skirt rather than Body Kit, which will keep it out of body kit collections and storefront filters. Owner decision: retype it, and note the Vigo is a Thai and Australia truck, so it earns its place in the AUS market only.
Toyota MR-S ZZW304442211000220004 sheet kits resolve to 4 true kits after splitting the FACTORY block into skirt kit + widebody and merging the Gemballa Mirage front bumper into the Porsche Carrera GT conversion. Everything exists on the site: 2 kits complete, the Carrera GT conversion is fragmented across two products and missing Fender Well 1338, and the 997 tail light kit sells 1 of its 3 pieces. Two drafts (Aero Kit, Full Kit) are copies of the Carrera GT product and should be archived after the side step is moved. Owner decision: whether the Gemballa Mirage front stays a standalone SKU or becomes the front bumper option inside the conversion kit.
Toyota MR2 SW20445240000000030Cleanest chassis in the group: 4 sheet kits, 4 true kits, all 4 live with every sheet piece present and zero duplicates. Only fixes are cosmetic - AB-FULK should read AB-Flug, and the single-piece Auto Pista listing should be titled Rear Spoiler rather than Body Kit. Two draft titanium products and the Rev5 wing have no sheet source, which is expected since they are not bodykit-sheet items.
Toyota Majesty111010000000000One sheet kit, one live product, all four pieces present, nothing missing or duplicated. Brand spelling is wrong (Aimgen should be Aimgain). Worth flagging commercially: the Majesty is a Thai-market van and ETi sells USA, AUS and EU, so this listing has almost no addressable audience. Owner decision: fix the brand name and decide whether the Thai-only vans stay in the storefront at all.
Toyota Soarer / Lexus SC300002000000000020No sheet rows exist for the Soarer / SC300 in this packet, so both store products are NO_SHEET_SOURCE by definition. The TOM'S kit has genuine components (Front Diffuser, Side Skirt, Complete) plus a matching TOM'S carbon hood, which suggests a real supplier kit filed elsewhere rather than junk. Owner decision: confirm where the Soarer rows live in the master sheet so the TOM'S kit can be checked for missing pieces such as a rear skirt.
Toyota Soluna110000001000000One sheet kit, zero store products: the Soluna is entirely missing from the catalog. The kit is small (TOM'S front lip plus side skirts, two molds) so building it is cheap. Commercially it is also the weakest case in this group: the Soluna is a Thai and Asia-only Tercel that was never sold in ETis USA, AUS or EU markets. Owner decision: leave it unbuilt unless a Thai wholesale channel opens.
Toyota Supra A900014000000070070A90 has zero sheet rows, so every product is NO_SHEET_SOURCE by definition (this bodykit sheet is MK4-era JDM kits; the A90 line comes from ETi's own moulds). The real issue is internal: 7 of 14 products sit in duplicate sets - three identical PRO front lips, two identical duckbill wings and two identical dry carbon wings - and the other-products block adds a third pair, door blades P10657636909337 vs P9753726877977. Owner decision: standardise on one naming convention (A90 vs MK5 vs MKV) and archive the older half of each pair, which removes five or six listings outright.
Toyota Vellfire111010000000000One sheet kit, one live product, all four pieces present. The single finding is a component mislabel that carries real money risk: the Wald door garnish set is listed simply as Door on a kit topping out at $2,805. Owner decision: rename the component to Door Garnish (6 pc) and add a photo showing the strips.
Toyota Wish1111111110000010000Sheet holds 11 real Wish kits and every one of them is live; nothing is missing and no kit is fragmented. The only structural problem is one draft clone of the ETi 6-piece skirt kit (P10657646117145). Housekeeping worth doing in one pass: Modellita to Modellista on two products, the bare Fender component to Rear Fender, and the Eye Line component name. Owner decision: archive the duplicate draft and lock the MC vs pre-MC split (codes 697-702 = facelift) so the two Ken Style and two Modellista listings stop looking like copies.
Toyota Yaris655140010000010Six auto-kits collapse to 5 true kits: K317 is only the full-bumper half of K318 and the store already sells them as one C-One Full RS product. Four of five kits are live and complete; the C-One skirt kit sits in draft and shares two molds with the live product. No missing pieces and no duplicates on this chassis. Owner decision: publish the C-One skirt draft as the cheaper lip option or archive it, and retitle the two single-piece listings (Ken Style spoiler) so they stop reading as body kits.
UNCLASSIFIED0002700000050051627 drafts, no sheet kits. Five are real catalog items filed under the wrong chassis: three Porsche 2009 drafts are the 997 Prior Design kit (K362) and two Porsche ETi GT1 drafts are the 987 GT1/GT3 RS widebody (K365), and the ETi GT1 Standard draft is the only itemized copy of that kit anywhere. Four more are real products with no sheet source (Voltex canards, two Ford Ranger parts, titanium wheel bolts) and one BMW Wide Body draft has no chassis at all. The remaining 17 are dropship novelties and a test product. Owner decision: harvest the two itemized Porsche drafts into their live listings, then bulk-archive the novelty drafts.
VW Beetle1100000010000001 sheet kit, zero store products. A complete 8-piece Rocket Bunny style Beetle widebody exists in mold and is unlisted, which is unusual given Rocket Bunny pulls traffic. Owner decision: confirm the RB attribution can be used publicly, then list it.

Mazda RX-7 FD3Smazda_rx7_fdThe 11 auto-kits resolve to 12 true kits: K101 splits into the Knight Sports spoiler+mirror set and the Minor Change 2000 (99+ facelift) bumper kit, and the store already got that split right. K106 (RE-Amemiya front bumper 1544) is the only fully missing kit; K103 Tokyo Drift is short its duckbill (live as its own product) and possibly the taillight panel, and K107 RE-Amemiya wide is short Rear Diffuser R+L (1551). Biggest naming problem: P10614301622553 is the standard RE-Amemiya AD kit but is titled and tagged 'wide body', colliding with the genuine wide kit P9080859754777. Duplicates are mild: 4 standalone or draft pieces repeat kit components (Mazdaspeed wing, RE street diffuser, RE GT canards, Vertex canard); 12 further products are legitimate non-sheet ETi or other-brand items.G08_mazda
Mazda RX-8 (SE3P)mazda_rx8Sheet holds 12 real RX-8 kits and no merges or splits were needed; 10 are live in some form, none is fully missing. Two are broken up: the R-Magic widebody V1 (K116) cannot be bought because its three fender pieces sit only in two duplicate drafts, and the ETi Minor Change R3 rear kit (K122) is split across two products. 14 of 39 store products are duplicates or duplicate components (5 draft clones of live items, plus VS-Style and MS-Style standalone pieces that repeat kit components), and 12 more are legitimate non-sheet items (trim, VTX1 pair, RB add-on set). Decision for the owner: publish the R-Magic V1 fenders into the live R-Magic product and archive the second widebody draft, then merge the two Minor Change products into one R3 kit.G08_mazda
Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution 7 / 8 / 9 (CT9A)mitsu_evo7_9Sheet holds 10 kits spanning three generations: Evo 7 (K130, K131), Evo 8 (K132-K136), Evo 9 (K137-K139). All 10 are live in some form, so nothing is MISSING, but the store is badly over-listed: 26 of the 67 products are drafts and 22 of those are straight copies of live listings. The Voltex Cyber Evo 9 kit (K138) alone is spread over nine products, and P10727222706457 is the only one carrying all 13 sheet pieces. Owner decision: name P10727222706457 the single Voltex master and archive the Time Attack duplicates, then rule on whether the 43-variant HKS Widebody kit is a real distinct mold set or the same Voltex tooling under another name.G07_mitsu
Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution X (CZ4A)mitsu_evo10Eight sheet kits collapse to six true kits: the EVO10 blocks K141, K143 and K145 are one aero program on shared molds 1133/1134/1136/1138/1167/001219 sold as Standard, Step 1 (no flares) and Step 2 (separate flares), not three kits. Nothing is MISSING, but the same kit occupies four products and three of its components (front fender, rear diffuser, front lip) are also loose standalone listings. Two single-piece sheet rows (Charge Speed roof 1139, Ralliart mirror 1148) are live as 'Body Kit' products and need retitling. Owner decision: collapse Standard/Step 1/Step 2 into one product with a Configuration option, then rule on the componentless $3,900 Wide Body Kit listing.G07_mitsu
Nissan 350Z Z33nissan_z3326 sheet kits collapse to 24 true kits: 18 are live and clean, 1 is fragmented (Amuse Superleggera widebody split across 3 products), 2 are partial (Weber Sport missing a second carbon rear spoiler, Face-Off 370Z missing rear diffuser 1262), 2 are missing outright (ETi front bumper 2030 and the whole Nismo 370 2017 conversion 3115/3116/3117/3418) and 2 need a ruling. The big structural problem is the ETi widebody 2026-2036: it is live TWICE under two wrong names (Nismo 2017 Style Wide Body Kit and Seido Style Widebody Kit) with 6 more Seido drafts fragmenting it, which also blocks the real Nismo 2017 conversion from ever being listed correctly. 5 draft copies duplicate live products (2 Amuse widebody, 1 louvers, 1 Seido widebody, 1 ducktail) and 2 active products are mislabeled shells (ETi Amuse Style Body Kit = louvers only, Top Secret Style Body Kit = one center diffuser). Owner decision: pick ONE identity for the 2026-2036 widebody (ETi, Nismo 2017 or Seido), then consolidate the Amuse Superleggera into a single 8-piece product and archive the 5 duplicate drafts.G04_z33_juke
Nissan 370Z Z34nissan_z3412 auto-kits settle into 14 true kits: K222 splits into the Amuse widebody add-on diffusers (1246-1248) and the FACTORY set (1257-1259), and K229 splits the W3 widebody from a customer-car engine bay cover set. Every sheet kit has a live product, so the problem here is duplication, not gaps: Allure is the Alluri W1 kit under a second name (plus a draft kit and 4 draft components), Raikou Style Kit duplicates Raikou W2, the Varis fender and the Duckbill Wing duplicate kit components, and Kaze Style Bodykit has no sheet source at all. Genuine holes: W3 rear diffuser (3137), the Nismo fender eyebrow pair collapsed into one option, and the engine bay covers (3171-3173) which are not listed anywhere. Decision for Nate: kill Allure and Kaze or map them to real kits, because the store currently sells the same ETi widebody under three names.G03_r34_z34
Nissan GT-R R35nissan_r3522 sheet kits collapse to 20 true kits (Liberty Walk body kit plus LB wing hardware = one; Fontier wing plus wing base = one) and all 20 are live, so nothing is missing or draft-only. Four kits are fragmented across two products each (Liberty Walk wing, Pandem duckbill, Top Secret Minor hood, Nismo Minor 2017) and only two pieces are genuinely absent: Tommy Kaira Bumper Intakes (1712) and Top Secret Front Plate CF (1692). The real mess is the legacy R35 GTR trim family: 18 drafts are straight copies of live products plus a Bensopra wing draft that duplicates a kit component, and 4 live standalone pieces duplicate kit components (Mine's duckbill, OEM rear spoiler, ZELE rear lip, Nismo bumper inlet); the same copy pattern exists in the hood list (draft P9851272331545 vs live P10658241511705). Owner decisions: retitle the nine single-piece listings still called Body Kit, rename the BenSopra component Hood to Hood Lock (3390) before someone buys a latch at hood money, and rule whether the unbranded Side Mirror Cover and Trunk Boot Lipspoiler are the same molds as the Nismo mirror (3157) and OEM spoiler (1064).G01_r35
Nissan S13 / 180SX / 200SXnissan_s13Sheet holds 14 auto-kits that settle into 15 true kits: K167 splits into Origin (983-985) and Minor (412-414), K174 splits into the ETi widebody (643-644) and the S15 face-off fenders (971-972), and K170+K171 merge into the JUN 180SX product. 13 of 15 are live and piece-complete, including the 16-piece S15 conversion and the 6-piece Nismo drift kit. Missing: Border front bumper 411 and the GP Sports drift pair 4022-4023. Duplicates: the ETi widebody exists three times (active canonical, active rear-fender-only, plus a draft), and the standalone rear diffuser overlaps the Minor kit. Owner decision: confirm whether the unattributed 200SX carbon front bumper is the Border 411 before anyone builds a second listing for it.G05_s_86
Nissan Silvia S14 (MC / kouki)nissan_s145 sheet kits, 5 true kits, all live and piece-complete: Standard fender, Bomex, D-Max widebody, C-West, Vertex. No missing pieces on this chassis. Two housekeeping problems: the Vertex kit is listed twice (a full 20-variant product and an old flat-priced copy) and the Standard fender is titled as a Body Kit. The Rocket Bunny S14 kit and its standalone front fender have no source in this sheet and duplicate each other. Owner decision: archive the legacy Vertex listing, and confirm what the Rocket Bunny S14 kit actually ships since the sheet cannot back it.G05_s_86
Nissan Silvia S15nissan_s156 sheet kits, 6 true kits: GP Sports, C-West conversion bumper, two Vertex canards, Vertex Lang, and the draft KRR fender. Five are live and piece-complete, KRR is draft-only at $0. Nothing is outright missing on this chassis. The real problem is naming: three products holding a single piece (two canards and the C-West bumper) are titled Body Kit, and the two canards look like the same product listed twice. Also present here are the two S13-sheet conversion products, the 16-piece S15 Conversion and the Face-Off fenders, both mapped clean. Owner decision: merge the two Vertex canards into one product with 1182 and 3190 as variants, and kill the Oats nickname in public copy.G05_s_86
Nissan Skyline R32nissan_r32Sheet holds 3 R32 kits (K232 GTR conversion, K233 Rocket Dancer, K234 Pandem race car) and all 3 are live and complete in one product each. The other 68 listings have no source in this bodykit sheet, most likely the GT-R wholesale and hoods lists, and that is where the mess is: 22 of 22 drafts are copies of live products, plus 4 listings of one GTS OEM front fender, 4 of the OEM front grille, 8 TS rear diffuser listings and 3 of the same GTR front bumper. Two brands are fragmented with no kit product, Vertex (4 standalone pieces) and Do-Luck (kit product plus 3 standalone copies), and the street Pandem kit has 3 stray draft singles. Owner decision: set one rule on selling kit components a-la-carte, then archive the ~26 duplicate drafts and build the Vertex kit product.G02_r32_r33
Nissan Skyline R33nissan_r33Sheet holds 3 R33 kits (K235 GTR, K236 BN-Sports, K237 400R side skirt). BN-Sports is live and complete, the GTR kit is missing one of its two spoiler molds (01514/1), and 400R is a single side skirt mis-titled as a Body Kit. All 14 drafts are copies of live products and should be archived, and the R33 front grille is listed three times. Do-Luck, JUN and Top Secret each have a full set of pieces on the site with no kit product to sell them as one. Owner decision: confirm whether P10658243641625 and P10658243576089 are the two K235 spoiler molds, then fix the 400R title and build the three missing kit products.G02_r32_r33
Nissan Skyline R34nissan_r34Sheet carries only 6 auto-kits for R34, which settle into 7 true kits: K242 splits into the GTR kit (766, 1573-1577) and the add-on GTR set (1578-1580, second rear diffuser proves the split). Six map cleanly to the 8-product sheet-derived cluster; the add-on set is FRAGMENTED because its 3-piece spoiler sits in a product titled Standard Body Kit, and the GTS (Blue) kit is missing front bumper 3370. The other 52 store products have no row in this bodykit sheet and are almost certainly the separate GT-R wholesale / hoods / wings lists.
